### Q1
No. The store stays a plain JSON file (data/store.json). Ops backs it up with a nightly rsync job that diffs plain-text files, and a binary SQLite file would break their backup checks. The performance fix is debounced writes plus a flush on shutdown.

### Q2
Yes: `src/legacy/` must not be modified. It is vendored from the old logistics monolith, and the platform team's sync job overwrites it every Monday, so any change would be silently lost. `docs/erp-api.md` is also off limits because the ERP team owns it.

### Q3
The signature goes in a top-level `sig` field in the JSON body. It is the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body without `sig`. Before that I used an `X-Signature` header, which failed because the ERP's API gateway strips custom X- headers, so every request looked unsigned.

### Q4
The ERP sandbox listens on port 9911 (since the October infra move). The README, docs/erp-api.md and the config/default.json default still say 8080.

### Q5
Every new user-facing error `message` must be in German, because warehouse packers see it verbatim in their UI. The `code` stays English SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.

### Q6
It uses a hardcoded list of Austrian public holidays for 2026 and 2027 in `src/services/holidays.ts`, and `isBusinessDay` checks it. It has no holiday API because the warehouse deployment has no outbound internet and has to work fully offline.

### Q7
No. The ERP answers 422 to any array payload, so it accepts only one event object per request. A teammate suggested batching, and the user had already tried it in September 2026.

### Q8
No new npm packages, runtime or dev. Every package needs a security review that takes about 6 weeks.

### Q9
Yes. I memoized `calculateEta` to speed up `GET /shipments`, and QA then reported stale ETAs after a new tracking event, because the cached value was never invalidated. I removed it completely, and the plan is to paginate the list endpoint later instead.

### Q10
Failed ERP calls get at most 3 attempts in total, with a fixed 30 s delay and no exponential backoff. The ERP only dedupes by event_id within a 2-minute window, so every attempt has to land inside it (worst case about 75 s). Only network errors and 5xx responses are retried, and the delay is injectable for tests.

### Q11
The recipient's name, address and phone number must never be logged, because of GDPR (the data protection officer flagged it in last month's audit). Shipment IDs and tracking numbers are fine to log.

### Q12
Yes: "emits webhook on delivered" in test/events.test.ts fails about 1 in 5 runs because of a timer race in the fake notifier (OPS-412, owned by the platform team). If it fails, rerun once and don't try to fix it.

### Q13
Only ATP numbers are validated, as UPU S10 including the check digit. All other carriers accept any non-empty value, because their formats change often and last year valid DHL numbers were wrongly rejected for 2 days.

### Q14
Hot reload is not built. `fs.watch` never fires on staging, because the config is a Docker bind mount from a Windows host and change events don't propagate into the container. `fs.watchFile` (polling) works, so that is the one to use.

### Q15
Yes: `GET /shipments/:id` must stay exactly as it is, with no added, removed or renamed fields. The mobile app v2.3 parses it with a strict schema and crashes on unknown or missing fields, and the next mobile release is in January 2027.
